title: Valence Shell, Valence Electron and Octet Theory
topicTitle: Valence shell, valence electron and octet theory
notes: **Valence shell:** the outermost electron shell of an atom. It determines the chemical bonding behaviour of the element.
**Valence electrons:** electrons in the valence shell. For main-group elements, these are the s and p electrons of the outermost shell.
**Octet theory (Lewis, 1916):** atoms tend to gain, lose or share electrons to achieve a stable outer shell of eight electrons (or two for hydrogen and helium).
**Why eight:** a full valence shell corresponds to the electron configuration of noble gases, which are chemically inert.
**Limitations:** octet theory fails for molecules with odd electrons (NO), expanded octets ($SF_6$), and electron-deficient compounds ($BF_3$).
